correctness.rationale: The primary paper's packet definition minimizes the size of a partition of the nontrivial base generators into sets of pairwise coprime orders with distinct superscripts (boxes). A cyclic normalizer quotient G/H has exactly one nontrivial base generator if d_H>1, of order d_H regardless of generator choice; trivial quotients contribute none. Acting in the representative orbit of a box leaves this count unchanged even when the box has several orbits. Distinct subgroups give distinct indices and the box restriction is automatic; packet classes are exactly color classes of the gcd conflict graph, also when the base set is empty. Private primes q_v distinguish types and guarantee nontrivial indices, while each edge prime p_e occurs exactly in its two endpoint indices. Thus the squarefree product construction realizes the input graph exactly. With one orbit per type, equivariance forbids different orbits being interchanged and each transitive cyclic orbit has automorphism group C_{d_v}; the product has one- or two-dimensional elementary abelian Sylow factors, with dimension two attained precisely when an edge exists. Projection provides the lower bound for rank and independent generating tuples across primes combine by CRT for the matching upper bound. For 6,10,15 the two stated generators are a basis modulo each of 2,3,5 on the respective two factors. In binary encoding the polynomial-size first-prime construction is polynomial time, and three-color witnesses are checked by gcd, divisibility and list validity without factoring. Appending a disjoint edge to the input leaves 3-colorability unchanged and forces rank exactly two. This is a many-one reduction on succinct data, not an explicit-point complexity result. The nested checker and expected output were inspected, not executed; the general proof does not depend on the finite enumeration.
residual_risks: The reported graph census and 900-element example are finite checks, not a fresh replay. The claimed restricted hardness concerns generated squarefree, rank-two instances; the NP-membership argument is for the stated binary-index decision problem.

value.rationale: This tests how informative the published coprime merging bound is, rather than inventing a packet parameter for a hard example. The obstruction is unbounded even for abelian unit groups of fixed rank two, and the encoding result shows that optimizing those packets can encode arbitrary three-colorability despite easy gcd checks and simple group structure. The contrast between true rank and a particular generation strategy is the useful structural conclusion.
residual_risks: Neither an explicit-permutation-table hardness result nor a claim that the actual rank is hard is supported.
